set.typical_award_size: Walnut Creek is a CDBG entitlement city in the Contra Costa HOME Consortium. FY 2026/27 (PY 2026-27) CDBG award $400,232 (FY 2025/26 $401,430), split by federal caps: $80,046 administration, $60,035 public services, $260,151 economic development, public facilities and housing. The City's Community Grant Program totals $1,050,232 for FY 2026/27 with local and state money: Community Services Grant $100,000, Homeless Services Grant $70,000, Measure O $250,000 (CORE outreach), General Fund $80,000 (school crisis counselors) and Prohousing Incentive Program $150,000; the City's PLHA grants that had funded homeless services are not available for FY 2026/27. The only housing activity funded is Habitat for Humanity home rehabilitation (about $82,350). The 2025-2029 Consolidated Plan estimates $2.12 million in federal resources over five years plus $4.14 million in general and local funds and programs $2.5 million for affordable housing (AH-1). FY 2025/26 was a competitive application year and FY 2026/27 a renewal year; the Consortium NOFA for the next three-year cycle was released October 15, 2026.
set.layering_notes: Walnut Creek's CDBG is small (about $400,000 a year) and mostly funds services, job training and owner-occupied rehab; for development, the City's Local Housing Trust Fund RFP (separate record) and County HOME or Measure X (county records) carry the weight, with HOME requests filed through the same Consortium application the County administers. Davis-Bacon applies to CDBG-assisted projects of 8 or more units. walnutcreekca.gov still returns 403 (Akamai) to scripts; award figures were read in the City's May 5, 2026 Council agenda report on the City's Granicus portal (walnutcreek.granicus.com, source_url), and Consortium NOFA dates and the Walnut Creek contact on the City of Antioch's Community Grants page (https://ca-antioch.civicplus.com/993/Community-Grants).

set.next_deadline: No application deadline; applies at entitlement. The Draft Zoning Code Update public review period runs October 22 through November 21, 2026 per the City Title 17 page (the draft's cover lists November 22, 2026); comments to planning@manteca.gov. As of November 15, 2026 the Planning Commission public hearing notice and General Plan Update EIR Addendum are listed on the City page without links, the City's Environmental and Public Hearing Notices page lists no Zoning Code Update hearing, and the November 19, 2026 Planning Commission meeting is cancelled; no hearing or adoption date is stated.
set.layering_notes: Manteca's 2011 chapter has not kept pace with state law (no 50% or 100% bonus tiers, old parking ratios), so state law controls in practice. The October 2026 public review draft of the Zoning Code Update keeps the same four eligibility thresholds (10% lower income, 5% very low income, senior, 10% moderate for-sale), shortens 17.72 to purpose, eligibility and approval sections, makes the City Council the approving authority for density bonuses and concessions, keeps the density bonus agreement, and lists the state findings needed to deny a concession; it does not write in the newer state tiers or parking caps, so state law will still control after adoption. Current Section 17.72.030.G still references a Chapter 17.32 Affordable Housing Requirements that no longer exists in the code (see next record). Manteca has no local trust fund, in-lieu fund or NOFA, so the land-use incentive plus County and regional sources (Urban County CDBG and HOME, SJRHF, HACSJ PBVs, BHSA) are the whole local layer. Current Chapter 17.72 was read on the official ecode360 host (source_url); the City's Title 17 page confirms the update schedule.
